page: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server configured with a single AMD EPYC 7443P processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU provides 24 physical cores and 48 threads running at a base clock of 2.85 GHz. The platform includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, delivering 5.33 GB of RAM per hardware thread. Local storage is supplied via a bundled 960 GB solid-state drive (SSD). The server contains zero GPUs and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark measurements show strong multi-threaded compute capability and high memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-tier single-core compute performance and registers within the top 25 percent in multi-core metrics with a score of 77,709.84. Geekbench testing reflects a multi-core score of 16,781.0, paired with strong results in software compilation via Clang (40,052.0) and ray tracing (55,688.0). PassMark testing places the overall CPU score at 60,061.01 and marks the memory score within the top 10 percent at 3,105.89. In cryptographic operations, hardware instruction support yields strong throughput across AES and SHA-NI workloads.

Operating as a bare metal platform, the server eliminates hypervisor virtualization overhead and noisy-neighbor interference. The balance of 48 dedicated execution threads and 256 GB of memory provides substantial resource density without the cost profile of specialized accelerator hardware. A key tradeoff is the 960 GB SSD capacity, which may require external volume attachments for storage-intensive applications. The hardware profile fits multi-threaded software compilation, container orchestration nodes, continuous integration pipelines, database management systems, and small-model CPU inference.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 7443P processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system delivers 24 physical cores and 48 threads clocked at 2.85 GHz, accompanied by 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz and a bundled 960 GB SSD. Without virtualization overhead or hardware GPUs, it provides direct hardware access and predictable compute density. Benchmark results show strong multi-core processing performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics placing in the top 25 percent. The memory subsystem also achieves top-tier PassMark memory scores. While the 960 GB SSD limits local bulk data retention, the configuration offers balanced resource allocation per core. This architecture is well suited for CPU-intensive compilation, containerized application clusters, high-concurrency database workloads, and CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference.
